old: Its name pairs a common girl's nickname with an old word for a noisy bird, as if calling out a talkative woman.
The second half once stood alone as the word for this bird, borrowed through French from a Latin term for it.

clues: This bird's name is basically an old joke about a gossipy woman: a personal nickname once used to mean a chatterer was added to an older word for the bird.
A noisy, long-tailed relative of the crow with bold black-and-white plumage, unlike the all-black crow or jackdaw, and famous in folklore for stealing shiny objects.
Someone who compulsively collects bright trinkets gets called one of these. Its name replaced older native English words for the bird, one of which survives as haggister.
